changelog: Rewrote [When to Segment] to explicitly forbid boundaries inside incomplete coordinate structures (X and Y, X or Y) until all coordinates close, and inside prepositional phrases (head + 'of'/'for'/'to' + object) until the object arrives. Added rule: do not mark before negations, reversals, or scope modifiers ('only', 'not', 'without', 'partially') that qualify or overturn the preceding claim.

Expanded [Never Segment] with three new prohibitions: (1) inside coordinate structures before the final coordinate arrives; (2) after a noun that heads a prepositional phrase, before the preposition's object; (3) before negations, exclusive markers, or scope-limiting modifiers that reverse or restrict the preceding assertion.

Reorganized [Priority Rules] to rank boundaries after COMPLETE coordinate structures and after polarity-settled clauses (with negation or reversal fully visible) as highest confidence. Demoted boundaries before unresolved modifiers, incomplete prepositional phrases, and polarity reversals to lowest confidence.

Added concrete examples to [When to Segment] showing where NOT to cut: 'X and Y' (cut after Y, not after X); 'head of object' (cut after object, not after head); 'claim + negation' (cut after negation, not after claim).
Clarified in [Priority Rules] that 'polarity settled' means the negation, reversal, or exclusive marker has already arrived and is visible in the emitted text, so the reader cannot be misled.
